item.title: EU to Call for European Security Council in New Defense Strategy
item.description: The European Union will propose creating a new security architecture with like-minded allies to confront growing defense threats amid doubts about US President Donald Trump’s commitments toward the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Valero and Andrea Palasciano

item.title: Markets Brace for First US Fed Hike Since 2023
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Bond traders have piled into bearish positions ahead of Wednesday’s Federal Reserve meeting, betting that the Treasury selloff driving yields to their highest in almost two decades will continue.
OpenAI is holding early talks with investors about a fresh funding round that would value company at more than $1.2 trillion ahead of an IPO. Senior Trump administration officials met Tuesday with Anthropic’s top Washington executive to discuss AI safety risks.
Today's guest: Luis Garicano, Rhine Group, Executive Director & London School of Economics Professor. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Europe Has Lost Race for Frontier AI Models, Says Rhine Group's Garicano
item.description: Luis Garicano, Rhine Group Executive Director, tells Bloomberg TV that Europe has lost the race for frontier AI models, but the region can still do the implementation side of the technology. The Rhine Group, Mario Draghi's new forum for tackling Europe's competitiveness challenges, brings together economists, industry and financial leaders, to build on the landmark report the former ECB President published two years ago. Garicano was speaking ahead of European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen delivering her annual State of the Union address at the European Parliament in Strasbourg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Federal Reserve Expected to Raise Interest Rates
item.description: The Federal Reserve is expected to hike interest rates on Wednesday for the first time since 2023. Bond traders have piled into bearish positions ahead of the Fed meeting. Bloomberg's Ven Ram breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Can Supercharge Putin’s Goals, Not His Great-Power Ambitions
item.description: While Russia lags in the race to develop cutting edge models — a contest dominated by the US and China — Moscow has become adept at co-opting AI for real-life situations.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: German Far Right Expects Power in Eastern State Sooner or Later
item.description: Germany’s far-right party is counting on surging support among voters to help it break through the firewall that the country’s established parties still hope will prevent it from taking power at state level for the first time since World War II.
item.dc:creator: Kamil Kowalcze

item.title: Houthi Conflict Threatens Saudi Arabia's Economy
item.description: The US-Iran war has reached crisis point for Saudi Arabia and its de facto leader, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, as the Houthis started firing at the kingdom on a near-daily basis this month. The hostilities had already pushed Saudi oil production to the lowest level in decades and they now threaten to complicate the kingdom’s multi-trillion dollar plans to diversify the economy. Bloomberg's Onur Ant reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hong Kong Vows to Deepen Role as Premier Offshore Yuan Hub
item.description: Hong Kong aims to deepen its role in promoting yuan use across financing, investment and trade, and will set up a mechanism to strengthen currency liquidity, its chief executive said in a policy speech.
item.dc:creator: Iris Ouyang

item.title: Germany's Hospitals Prepare for War and Mass Casualties as Russia Threat Looms
item.description: At first glance, the hospital in the southwestern German city of Ulm looks much like any other. Patients sit in reception areas waiting to be called, doctors roam the halls looking at reports or their phones. Only the uniformed soldiers among the staff hint at military ties. Yet many meters beneath its busy wards lies a Cold War-era bunker that has suddenly become relevant again.
item.dc:creator: Sonja Wind

item.title: Swiss Set to Reject Stricter Neutrality Rules, Final Polls Show
item.description: Swiss voters are set to reject a proposal to tighten the country’s neutrality this month, preserving the government’s freedom to interpret the doctrine flexibly.
item.dc:creator: Bastian Benrath-Wright

item.title: UK Should Slash Tax on Rich, Blueprint for Farage’s Reform Says
item.description: The UK should slash taxes on the rich and encourage the City to take greater risks, according to a report by a think-tank linked to Reform UK that’s set to guide the economic policies of Nigel Farage’s insurgent party.
item.dc:creator: Katherine Griffiths, Harry Wilson and Lucy White

item.title: Marcos Cousin Romualdez Pleads Not Guilty of Plundering Flood Project Funds
item.description: The lawmaker cousin of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. pleaded not guilty to a plunder charge in a corruption scandal involving flood control projects.
item.dc:creator: Neil Jerome Morales

item.title: Live Blog: Hong Kong's John Lee Unveils First Ever Five-Year Plan
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: US Plans to Provide Thousands of Massive Weapons to Israel
item.description: The US is preparing to provide Israel thousands of bombs that are among the most destructive in its arsenal, the largest single transfer of such weapons in years.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride and Tony Capaccio

item.title: Takaichi Projects Power in Cabinet Reshuffle Before US Trip
item.description: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is poised to keep her core team in place in a customary reshuffle nearly a year after taking office, showing renewed confidence after weathering market turmoil and coalition frictions.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiaki Nohara

item.title: US Senate Blocks Clarity Act Crypto Bill
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Troy Downing (R-MT) says that proposed $5,000 checks could add to the deficit and fuel inflation as he raises concerns about the plan’s price tag. Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says that he expects Leon Black will be held in contempt after the House Oversight Committee panel voted to advance the matter to the full House. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Krishnamoorthi Says Leon Black Vote May Be Unanimous
item.description: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says that he expects Leon Black will be held in contempt after the House Oversight Committee panel voted to advance the matter to the full House. Rep. Krishnamoorthi says that he expects to support the Russia sanctions bill even though it would give President Trump additional tariff authority, arguing that more pressure is needed on Russia’s oil revenues. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Downing Says Fed Has No Choice But To Raise Rates
item.description: Rep. Troy Downing (R-MT) says that proposed $5,000 checks could add to the deficit and fuel inflation as he raises concerns about the plan’s price tag. Rep. Downing says that the Federal Reserve has “no choice” but to raise rates with inflation still above target and expects a modest increase. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brazil Top Court Puts Off Moraes Decision, Clouding Election
item.description: Brazil’s Supreme Court delayed a decision on whether to open an unprecedented investigation into one of its justices after a tense public hearing in which members traded accusations of political bias and spreading falsehoods about each other.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho, Martha Beck and Beatriz Reis

item.title: Indonesian Power Politics, Not Just Markets, Forced Out Finance Chief Purbaya
item.description: The end came quickly for Indonesia’s finance minister.
item.dc:creator: Grace Sihombing, Chandra Asmara, Harry Suhartono, Prima Wirayani, Norman Harsono and Rieka Rahadiana
